The metamaterial unit cell consists of a single-gap SRR printed on a Rogers 5880 substrate with a Teflon slab backing.
Typical unit cell dimensions are 1.354 mm × 5 mm × 5 mm with copper wire thickness t=0.06 mm.
The resonance frequency (f0) and magnetic plasma frequency (fp) are key parameters characterizing the SRR's magnetic response.
Increasing the gap size s from 0.1 mm to 0.65 mm raises f0 from 7.20 GHz to 8.54 GHz and fp from 8.05 GHz to 9.51 GHz.
Increasing the copper wire width w from 0.22 mm to 0.40 mm lowers f0 from 8.63 GHz to 7.44 GHz and fp from 9.54 GHz to 8.48 GHz.
Increasing the copper wire lengths ly and lz similarly decrease resonance frequencies.
Increasing copper wire thickness t from 0.06 mm to 0.12 mm decreases f0 from 8.40 GHz to 7.57 GHz and fp from 9.54 GHz to 8.61 GHz.
The effective permeability at 9.5 GHz can be tuned from near zero to about 0.5 by adjusting SRR geometry.
The designed invisibility cloak consists of 10 concentric cylindrical layers with radii from 27.1 mm to 83.18 mm.
Each cloak layer uses SRR unit cells with specific geometric parameters to achieve the required radial permeability gradient.
The cloak operates for TE polarization with electric field parallel to the cylinder axis.
Transformation optics compresses the original cylindrical region into a hollow shell, requiring spatially varying permeability and permittivity.
The azimuthal permeability µh is set to unity and axial permittivity εz is constant at 2.2 for practical realization.
The magnetic resonance frequency of the SRR unit cell is approximately 8.4 GHz, with a low-loss band around 9.5 GHz.
The S-parameters retrieval method is used to extract effective permeability from simulated scattering parameters.
The resonance band shifts to higher frequencies with increasing gap size and to lower frequencies with increasing wire width and length.
The thickness of the copper wires affects both the resonance frequency and the bandwidth of the magnetic response.
The cloak design ensures minimal scattering and reflection, rendering the interior region electromagnetically invisible.
The SRR unit cells are subwavelength in size, less than 1/10 of the free-space wavelength at 9.5 GHz.
The study confirms that geometric tuning of SRRs enables practical metamaterial designs for microwave invisibility cloaks.
